studies.label: Wave 1 lab experiment (HI vs HAT vs HHT), picture-idea tasks 2 and 3
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Robust standard errors are clustered by experimental session (PDF p. 8, Table 3; PDF p. 18, Appendix C). The session counts in clusters_per_arm are observed sessions from Table D.2, not proof of session randomization. Sessions contain participants and their repeated outputs, but individual versus session allocation and the random-effects grouping are not explicitly established. se_basis is unclear pending the allocation protocol; it is not coded output merely because the outcome rows are ideas.

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 2, Section 1; PDF p. 19, Table D.2 (columns Training, HAT, HI, HHT); exclusions in PDF p. 17, Appendix B.2
counts_source.quote: In the ﬁrst wave, 246 participants were recruited and randomly assigned to one of three between-subject treatments. ... No. subjects 56 61 63 122 No. sessions 2 2 2 5

arms.name: HI (Control)
arms.description: Human individual: treated picture-idea tasks alone without ChatGPT (PDF p. 4). All arms first received the same brief ChatGPT familiarization.

arms.name: HAT
arms.description: Human-AI team: individual participant may chat freely with ChatGPT 3.5 through Poe.com while producing picture ideas (PDF pp. 4, 6).

arms.name: HHT
arms.description: Human-human team: anonymous pairs, randomly re-matched for each treated task, converse by text and submit a shared idea (PDF p. 4).

studies.task: Nankai University students describe a creative picture in fewer than 100 Chinese characters within a 12-minute soft time limit for each of two counterbalanced themes; experimenters later generate images from the descriptions (PDF pp. 5-6).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT 3.5 accessed through poe.com
ai_tool.locator: PDF pp. 4, 6, Sections 2.1 and 2.3. First-wave deployment was May-June 2023; model release year is not stated. DALL-E 3 via ChatGPT-4o was used by experimenters to render outputs, not supplied to participants (PDF p. 17).

preregistration.where: AsPredicted.org; PDF p. 6, Section 2.3. Registration and deviations are in Supplementary Section 1, not on file.

studies.shared_sample: Earlier working paper Zhu and Zou (2023), The role of generative AI in human creative processes: experimental evidence, SSRN 4676053, used the same first-wave participants with an earlier evaluation panel (PDF p. 2, footnote 2; PDF p. 22). The citation record also identifies SSRN 5196748 as a version; its overlap is not separately established in this PDF.

not_extracted.what: S2: all Training-cohort outcomes S2-O1 through S2-O7, including Training versus HI, HAT, or HHT
not_extracted.reason: Nonrandom comparison with separately recruited first-wave arms. Sections 1 and 2.1 (PDF pp. 3, 5) explicitly discuss time-lag and sample-selection limitations; the generic random-distribution statement in Appendix B.2 does not resolve the contradiction.

not_extracted.what: S3: Standalone ChatGPT versus human or human-AI outputs (PDF p. 12; Tables D.4-D.5, PDF p. 20)
not_extracted.reason: The AI-only arm contains no person receiving assistance. Human-arm descriptive cells are retained separately without importing model-only comparison tests.

not_extracted.what: Hypothetical human-AI and human-human team benchmarks (PDF p. 12, Section 4.1)
not_extracted.reason: Simulated pairings and mechanically selected maxima are not randomized groups of people who worked in those conditions.

not_extracted.what: S1-O4: Post-treatment original DAT score
not_extracted.reason: Output-scored original DAT measures within-person flexibility, but AI availability during the post-task test is unstated (PDF pp. 4, 16-17), so with_ai versus after_ai cannot be confirmed. Figure 4b has no numerical coefficient or interval endpoints (PDF p. 11); PDF p. 12 reports a nonsignificant effect. Its model also adjusts for unbalanced controls, including major collected in final Questionnaire III (PDF pp. 8, 11, 16, 18), and is excluded under rule 5. No figure values are estimated.

not_extracted.what: S1-O5: Post-treatment modified-DAT score
not_extracted.reason: Output-scored modified DAT measures novelty relative to supplied words (PDF pp. 16-17). AI availability during the post-task test is unstated, preventing with_ai/after_ai classification. PDF p. 12, Section 3.4, prints: experiencing ChatGPT access and experiencing teamwork both lead to an increase of 0.19 SDs in the modiﬁed-DAT score; The Figure 4b model also adjusts for unbalanced controls, including major collected in final Questionnaire III (PDF pp. 8, 11, 16, 18), and is excluded under rule 5. Exact raw coefficients, SEs and analyzed-person counts are absent; no figure values are estimated.

notes: Reconciled 2026-10-10. Read all 115628 characters of the markdown in contiguous chunks, including appendices and references, then extracted every PDF page with pymupdf and checked relevant table layouts. The PDF page index plus one equals its printed page number. Only extraction/c150.json was written. Rule 5 is applied to measurement timing as written: major and drawing-AI experience were elicited in final Questionnaire III, so all models adjusting for either are excluded even when they describe prior characteristics. This removes Table 3 columns (2),(3),(5),(6), Table 7 baselines, Table 8, and Table D.3 noninteraction results, as well as mediator and moderator models. Table 3 columns (1) and (4) and printed descriptive arm summaries remain eligible. Image-text is the published-paper primary outcome; the retained no-participant-covariate model is the eligible pooled-theme specification. All retained counts, question, construct, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai and within_person fields were checked independently of extractor agreement. All retained outcomes concern outputs made with ChatGPT available to HAT. Quality grades are overall_creativity at output level; inequality indices are other at set level and higher means more inequality. Theme-specific summaries use the same assigned groups, not subgroups or first-round-only samples. Counts remain null unless directly printed for that analysis. No counts, differences, SDs, standardized effects or intervals were calculated. Raw arm summaries from the discarded main-model records were transferred to the corresponding eligible model records. The scripts mismatched several analyses: only_in_b theme records also exist in A under different slugs. None of the retained outcomes or contrasts is new to both extractors; n_added is zero. All model variants and descriptive records share the same first-wave sample. No across_people outcome is reported. Supplement retrieval failed without saving any downloaded files. The resolutions cover every distinct study/estimate field difference and each script-only entry; the diff repeats n_units within eight mismatched pairs, and each repeated occurrence is represented by its single field resolution. Numeric p-value bounds preserve the printed leading-decimal notation.
